data.narrative:
Type One Energy, a Series B nuclear energy company that has raised $100M+, operates within a fragmented frontier-tech sector comprising 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private competitors including Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy. The narrow peer set reflects the nascent stage of advanced nuclear deployment.

Stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach, anchors valuation to the $100M total raised proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B progression. This yields an implied valuation of $190M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints—while 5 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 meet narrow filters for stage, tier, and capital structure alignment, making extrapolation from the broader peer universe unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, centered on $190M. Key uncertainties center on the absence of sufficiently granular comparable transaction data within advanced nuclear, limiting conviction in stage-progression multiples. Refinement would require either (a) disclosure of recent financings within the nuclear cohort at comparable stages, or (b) expansion into adjacent hard-tech sectors with similar capital intensity and regulatory constraints. Until such data emerges, the $190M median reflects methodological constraints rather than high confidence precision.
